subChunks.title: Borders, Rings, and Rounded Corners
subChunks.hookHtml: Borders, outlines, and rounded corners are the visual scaffolding of every UI component. Tailwind's border utilities give you per-side control, colour, and radius in a consistent naming system — plus the ring utility for accessible focus indicators that never interfere with layout.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Border width

border       /* 1px border all sides */
border-2     /* 2px border all sides */
border-4     /* 4px border all sides */
border-8     /* 8px border all sides */
border-0     /* remove border        */

/* Per-side */
border-t     /* top only    */
border-r     /* right only  */
border-b     /* bottom only */
border-l     /* left only   */
border-x     /* left + right */
border-y     /* top + bottom */

Border colour

border-gray-200   /* light separator */
border-gray-300   /* visible input border */
border-blue-500   /* active/focus state */
border-red-500    /* error state */
border-transparent

Border style

border-solid    /* default  */
border-dashed
border-dotted
border-none

Rounded corners

rounded-none   /* 0 */
rounded-sm     /* 2px  */
rounded        /* 4px  (default) */
rounded-md     /* 6px  */
rounded-lg     /* 8px  */
rounded-xl     /* 12px */
rounded-2xl    /* 16px */
rounded-3xl    /* 24px */
rounded-full   /* 9999px — pill/circle */

/* Per-corner */
rounded-tl-lg  /* top-left only */
rounded-tr-lg  /* top-right only */
/* etc. */

Ring (focus indicator)

Rings use box-shadow — they appear outside the element without affecting layout:

ring           /* 3px ring */
ring-2         /* 2px ring */
ring-4         /* 4px ring */
ring-blue-500  /* ring colour */
ring-offset-2  /* gap between element and ring */

/* Focus ring pattern for accessible buttons/inputs: */
focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:ring-offset-2 focus:outline-none

Divide: borders between siblings

<ul class="divide-y divide-gray-100">
  <li class="py-3">Item 1</li>
  <li class="py-3">Item 2</li>  <!-- border-top applied -->
</ul>

Lyra: "Rings are the preferred focus indicator in Tailwind. Unlike outlines, they respect border-radius and sit outside the element without disturbing layout. Always use ring on interactive elements — it is the difference between an accessible and an inaccessible UI."

storyBeats.speaker: Lyra the Scribe
storyBeats.text: Every container has an edge. The question is how visible that edge should be. A separator in a list? border-b border-gray-100 — barely there. An input that needs user attention? border-2 border-blue-500 — unmistakable. And when a user focuses the input? ring-2 ring-blue-500 ring-offset-2 — outside the border, never displacing layout.

storyBeats.speaker: Input states with borders and rings
storyBeats.text:
<!-- Default input -->
<input class="border border-gray-300 rounded-lg px-3 py-2" />

<!-- Error state -->
<input class="border-2 border-red-500 rounded-lg px-3 py-2" />

<!-- Focus state (via :focus variant) -->
<input class="border border-gray-300 rounded-lg px-3 py-2
              focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:ring-offset-1" />

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Style a member card with borders and focus indicators: a card container with a visible border and rounded corners. A list of members inside separated by horizontal dividers. A 'Join Guild' button with no border by default but a blue ring when focused (use focus: prefix).
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain why Tailwind's ring utility uses box-shadow rather than CSS outline — what is the practical difference when it comes to border-radius and layout impact? When would you use divide-y vs adding border-b to each child individually?

questions.prompt: Which class creates a full-circle or pill shape from any element?
questions.explanation: rounded-full applies border-radius: 9999px, which creates a circle on square elements and a pill on rectangular ones. It's the standard for avatar images, badge chips, and toggle switches.

questions.prompt: You want an accessible focus indicator on a button that doesn't affect layout and respects the button's border-radius. Which class string achieves this?
questions.explanation: Ring uses box-shadow, which sits outside the element without affecting layout or clipping to overflow:hidden. focus:outline-none removes the browser default outline, and the ring replaces it. ring-offset-2 adds a 2px gap between the element and the ring — important for dark backgrounds.

questions.prompt: You have a list of items and want a 1px separator between each item but not before the first or after the last. Which approach is most maintainable?
options: divide-y divide-gray-100 on the parent — Tailwind adds a top border to every child except the first
border-b border-gray-100 on every list item
mt-px bg-gray-100 on a separate <hr> element between items
space-y-px on the parent — it adds 1px gaps between children
questions.answer: divide-y divide-gray-100 on the parent — Tailwind adds a top border to every child except the first
questions.explanation: divide-y adds a top border to every child except the first using the CSS sibling selector (* + *). Adding border-b to every item requires managing the last-child exception yourself. divide-y is idiomatic Tailwind for list separators and is easier to change (one class on the parent vs. touching every child).
